# OER Project Log: Authorship & AI

*This document generated by Claude Sonnet 4.6 based on my notes*

## Project Context

Working toward submission of the **Nancy Tannery Grant for OER** (deadline: March 18, 2026). Project involves creating a modular set of 8–12 OER modules on generative AI integration in academic writing instruction, for immediate use in Fall 2026 "Authorship & AI" course and adaptable across other writing-intensive courses (INFSCI 2205, ESL writing, etc.). Materials to be released under CC-BY license.

## Session: 2026-02-28

### Goal

Identify and set up a publishing infrastructure for the OER that aligns with the project's stated workflow: Markdown source files, public GitHub repo, version control, multi-format output (HTML for Canvas, PDF for print).

### What Was Done

**Evaluated Lantern as the publishing platform.**

-   Lantern (https://github.com/nulib-oer/lantern) is a minimal-computing OER publishing toolkit developed at Northwestern.
-   Uses Markdown + YAML as source formats — non-proprietary, plain text, human-readable, version-controllable with Git.
-   Integrates Pandoc under the hood to convert source files to multiple output formats (HTML, PDF, EPUB, etc.).
-   This matches the workflow already described in the grant application almost exactly — essentially the same architecture that was planned for independent construction, but pre-configured.
-   Reviewed the Lantern wiki: https://github.com/nulib-oer/lantern/wiki

**Created personal repository from the Lantern template.**

-   Repository: https://github.com/billcprice3/authorship-and-ai
-   Status: Initial commit only. No content added. No configuration changes made yet.

### Where Things Stand

The repo exists and is ready for the next phase of setup. Nothing has been tested yet — no content files added, no build process run, no output formats generated. The Lantern wiki documents the full workflow from manuscript to publication and will serve as the guide for next steps.
